newsitem.title: UK: Blair, Clinton plan G7 jobs initiative - officials.
newsitem.headline: Blair, Clinton plan G7 jobs initiative - officials.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton and British Prime Minister Tony Blair are planning a joint initiative under the umbrella of the Group of Seven to tackle unemployment, British officials said on Thursday.

They said they would ask other members of the G7 at next month's summit in Denver to launch a plan aimed at reducing joblessness in industrial countries by increasing labour market flexibility and reducing the burdens on business.
Britain, which will take over the rotating chairmanship of the G7 after the United States, is planning a special summit of the Seven in London next January on the issue, officials said.
Blair and Clinton were expected to announce details of the initiative at a news conference on Thursday afternoon following talks at Blair's Downing Street residence.

Britain and the United States believe the rest of the Group of Seven -- Japan, France, Germany, Italy and Canada -- can learn from their success in creating jobs by keeping labour costs low and cutting through red tape to encourage small firms.
It was not immediately clear whether the planned January summit would be attended by heads of government or by ministers.
G7 employment ministers have held two job summits in recent years, one in Detroit and the other in Lille.
